transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, what brought me in is... people keep telling me I’m not listening to them. 

My supervisor at work, or my wife, they'll be talking straight to me, and... a minute later I realize I only caught about half of it. Then I'm stuck asking them to say it all over again. It's been causing some problems, so I figured I should come in.
Have you found yourself getting distracted easily or having trouble focusing on tasks, even when you're trying to pay attention?

I don't really think so. When I'm working on the floor, I just do my job. I haven't really noticed getting distracted from my actual tasks. It's really just what I said before—when people are standing there talking to me, that's when I miss things. But focusing on the work itself... no, I wouldn't say I have trouble with that.
When people are talking to you, do you find yourself getting anxious or worried about what they might think of you, which makes it harder to focus on what they're saying?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really get nervous or worry about what people think of me. It's not an anxiety thing. I just... I don't know, my brain just sort of goes somewhere else while they're talking. But I'm definitely not sitting there stressing over their opinion of me or anything like that.
Outside of conversations, do you find yourself losing focus or your mind wandering, for example, when reading, watching something, or listening to a lecture?

Not really, no. I mean, I don't read much, and I definitely don't go to lectures. But if I'm just watching TV or a movie at home, I follow it fine. I haven't noticed my mind wandering off then. It really is just... like I said, mostly when someone is standing there talking right at me.
When you're watching TV or a movie, are there times when you realize you weren't really paying attention, even though you were looking at the screen?

No, I don't think so. If I'm sitting down to watch a show or a movie or something, I'm pretty focused on it. I don't really get that thing where you're just staring at the screen but not actually taking it in. Like I was saying, I follow it fine.
Have you ever found yourself zoning out or not paying attention when someone is talking to you in a group setting, like during a meeting or while watching something together?

No, not really. If I'm in a group or a meeting at work, I'm usually pretty tuned in. It's really just when it's one-on-one, like someone talking directly to my face, that I kind of drift off. But in a group, no, I don't really have that problem.
Can you describe what happens when someone is talking to you one-on-one? Do you notice your mind wandering off, or do you feel disengaged even though you're trying to listen?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Honestly, that's what brought me in here in the first place. People just keep saying I'm not listening. 

My supervisor at work, or my wife... they'll be standing there talking straight to me, and I think I'm paying attention. But then a minute later, I realize I only caught half of what they actually said. I just kind of drift off without meaning to, and then I end up having to ask them to say it all over again.
When you're talking one-on-one and you find yourself drifting off, do you ever feel detached from yourself or like you're watching the conversation from outside your body?

No, I don't get anything like that. I don't feel outside my body or anything weird. I just... stop hearing them. Like my brain just changes the channel for a second, but I'm still right there in the room.
Have you ever heard sounds or voices that others don't seem to hear, or had the sense that something you were perceiving wasn't quite real, especially when you're tuning out during a conversation?
No, definitely not. I don't hear voices or anything that isn't there. When I tune out, it's just my own normal thoughts distracting me, not anything imaginary or weird like that.
When you're drifting off during a conversation, do you ever feel like you're not fully aware of what's happening around you, even after the conversation has ended?

No, I wouldn't say that. Once the conversation is over, or once I realize I missed something, I'm fully aware of what's going on around me. I don't feel out of it or confused about where I am. It's just that I missed what they were saying in that specific moment.
When you're tuning out during a conversation, do you ever find yourself daydreaming or seeing images in your mind that distract you, or is it just thoughts that pull your attention away?

No, I don't really see images or anything like that. It's not like I'm having a whole daydream where I'm picturing things. It's really just my thoughts going a mile a minute. I'll just start thinking about something I have to do later, or something that happened at work, and that's what pulls me away. It's just normal thoughts, just... too many of them at once, I guess.

When you realize you've missed part of a conversation, is it that you remember part of what was said but not all of it, or do you sometimes have no memory of what was said at all, like it just disappeared from your mind?

It's more like I just didn't hear it in the first place. I wouldn't say it disappears from my memory, because it never really registered. I'll catch the beginning of what they're saying, and then my mind just goes off on its own track. So when I snap back to it, I just have no idea what they were just talking about for those last few seconds or minutes.
Are there times outside of conversations when you feel like you're not fully present or aware of what's happening around you, even just for a few seconds?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm always pretty aware of where I am and what I'm doing. Even if I'm at work on the line and my mind is racing about a hundred different things, I still know I'm at work, you know? I don't just blank out or lose touch with my surroundings. It's really just that I get distracted by my own thoughts, but I'm not... I'm not disconnected from what's going on around me.

Have you ever experienced any strange or unusual sensations, like things looking or sounding different than they should, or feeling like things around you aren’t real, especially when you're not in a conversation?

No, I haven't ever had anything like that. Things always look and sound like they're supposed to. I definitely don't feel like things aren't real. Like I said, I'm always pretty aware of what's going on around me, it's just my brain moving too fast. But no weird sensations or anything feeling fake, no.
Outside of conversations, do you ever notice your thoughts racing so fast that it's hard to keep up with them, even when you're trying to focus on something else?

I mean, I know I used the word 'racing' a minute ago, but I wouldn't say they go so fast that I can't keep up with them. It's not really like that. 

It's more just that I'm thinking about a bunch of different things at the same time, like while I'm working the line or driving or whatever. But I always know what I'm thinking about. It doesn't feel out of control or moving too fast to follow. It's just... busy, I guess. So no, I haven't really noticed it being hard to keep track of my own thoughts.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized, unusually good or irritable, or like you didn’t need as much sleep as usual?

No, not really. I mean, I've never felt unusually good or anything like that. And my sleep is pretty much the same all the time. I get tired, I go to bed, I wake up. I don't have times where I feel like I don't need sleep. I might be restless a lot, but it's not like I'm running on empty and feeling fine about it. So no, I wouldn't say I've had anything like that.
